goal.users: Customers who want to see the menu and pre-order for pickup. The shop team receives the orders by email.
goal.problem: Customers of Brew Lab have no easy way to see the menu and prices or to order ahead and collect at the shop. The shop has no online page that shows its name and address.
features: Page shows the name Brew Lab and the address 12, 100 Feet Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038 as text, with no embedded map
Menu of seven items with prices in rupees
Pre-order form with fields name, phone, items and pickup time, sent to hello@brewlab.example
Pickup at the shop, with no online payment

user_groups.name: Customers
actions: View the shop name and address
Fill in and submit the pre-order form
Collect the order at the shop

constraints: No opening hours are shown (not decided yet)
No shop phone number is shown (the shop has none)
No details made up beyond the brief
Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file with no build step
The PRD, HLD, LLD and website must agree with each other

All seven menu items appear with the correct rupee prices
The pre-order form has exactly the fields name, phone, items and pickup time and sends to hello@brewlab.example
The page has no horizontal overflow at 360px width
The PRD, HLD, LLD and website contain the same facts with no contradictions

requirements.text: The page shows the name Brew Lab as text.
The page shows the address 12, 100 Feet Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038 as text, so customers can view the shop name and address.
The page has no embedded map. The address is the only location information on the page.
The menu lists exactly seven items: Filter coffee 90, Cappuccino 160, Latte 180, Cold brew 200, Masala chai 80, Almond croissant 140 and Banana bread slice 120.
Every menu price is in rupees and matches the number given in R4, so customers can read the menu and prices.
The page has a pre-order form with the fields name, phone, items and pickup time, and no other fields.
When the person ordering submits the pre-order form, the order is sent to hello@brewlab.example, where the Shop team receives it.
Customers collect the order at the shop.
No online payment is taken. The page has no payment fields.
The page works on phones, with no horizontal overflow at 360px width.
The page does not show opening hours or a shop phone number.
The page is one file of plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step, and it contains the same facts as the PRD, HLD and LLD with no contradictions.

W-8.body:
## Purpose and scope

This high-level design describes how the Brew Lab page is built to meet the PRD requirements R1 to R12. Brew Lab is a small specialty coffee shop at 12, 100 Feet Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038. Customers of Brew Lab have no easy way to see the menu and prices or to order ahead and collect at the shop, and the shop has no online page that shows its name and address. The page solves this.

**Purpose**
- Show the name Brew Lab and the address 12, 100 Feet Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038 as text.
- Show the menu of seven items with prices in rupees.
- Let customers send a pre-order through a form with the fields name, phone, items and pickup time. The form sends the order to hello@brewlab.example, where the Shop team receives it.
- Let customers collect the order at the shop.
- Work on phones, with no horizontal overflow at 360px width.

**In scope**
- One page, built as one file of plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step.
- The shop name and address as text.
- The menu with the seven items and their rupee prices.
- The pre-order form, with pickup at the shop.

**Out of scope**
- Opening hours (not decided yet), so none are shown.

**Users**

## Components

The Brew Lab page is made of eight components. Each has one responsibility and names the PRD requirements it covers, so every requirement R1 to R12 traces to a component.

- **C1** Shop identity block: shows the name Brew Lab and the address 12, 100 Feet Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038 as text, with no embedded map, so the address is the only location information. Covers R1, R2, R3.
- **C2** Menu list: shows exactly seven items with prices in rupees: Filter coffee 90, Cappuccino 160, Latte 180, Cold brew 200, Masala chai 80, Almond croissant 140 and Banana bread slice 120. Covers R4, R5.
- **C3** Pre-order form: collects the fields name, phone, items and pickup time, and no other fields. Covers R6.

W-11.body:
## Data flow

This section follows a pre-order from the customer to the Shop team. The page has one form and one destination for the order, hello@brewlab.example. It has no other integration, no map, no payment service and no database.

**Forms**
- The pre-order form (component C3, covers R6) is the only form on the page. Its fields are name, phone, items and pickup time, and no other fields.
- The phone field holds the phone number of the person ordering. It is not a shop phone number, and the page shows no shop phone number (R11).

**Integrations**
- Order delivery (component C4, covers R7) sends the submitted order to hello@brewlab.example, where the Shop team receives it.
- There are no other integrations. The page has no embedded map (R3) and takes no online payment (R9).

**Flow of a pre-order**
1. The customer reads the menu, where the seven items show their prices in rupees (R4, R5).
2. The customer fills in the form fields name, phone, items and pickup time.
3. The customer submits the form.
4. The order, with those four fields, is sent to hello@brewlab.example (R7).
5. The Shop team receives the order at hello@brewlab.example.
6. The customer collects the order at the shop (R8). The page takes no online payment and holds no payment fields, so no payment data moves anywhere (R9).

**Data carried**

| Data | Where it comes from | Where it goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | Customer, in the form | hello@brewlab.example |
| phone | Customer, in the form | hello@brewlab.example |
| items | Customer, in the form | hello@brewlab.example |
| pickup time | Customer, in the form | hello@brewlab.example |

**Not in the flow**
- Payment details: none are collected, because no online payment is taken.
- Opening hours and a shop phone number: none are shown (R11).
- The menu and the address are fixed text on the page. They are not sent anywhere.

Assumption: the form is submitted from the customer's own device, and the page does not send the order anywhere other than hello@brewlab.example.

W-12.body:
## Hosting and deployment

The Brew Lab page ships as one file of plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step (PRD R12, component C8). The file is the whole website, so there is nothing to compile, bundle or install before it goes live.

**What is deployed**
- One file holding the HTML, the CSS and the JavaScript of the Brew Lab page.
- The file holds the shop name Brew Lab, the address 12, 100 Feet Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038 as text, the menu of seven items with prices in rupees, and the pre-order form with the fields name, phone, items and pickup time.
- The file has no embedded map, no payment fields, no opening hours and no shop phone number.

**Where it lives**
- The brief and the PRD do not name a hosting provider, a domain or a cost, so this document names none and states no cost.
- The page is a fixed file, so any place that can serve one file to a browser can hold it. The page needs no server code of its own.

**How it ships**
1. The file is written as one file, with no build step.
2. The file is checked against the PRD: the same facts as the PRD, HLD and LLD, no contradictions (R12), the seven menu items and rupee prices (R4, R5), the form fields (R6) and no horizontal overflow at 360px width (R10).
3. The checked file is put in its place as it is. No other step changes it.
4. A change to the page is a change to this one file, which is checked again the same way before it replaces the earlier file.

**What the deployment depends on**
- The pre-order form sends the order to hello@brewlab.example, where the Shop team receives it (R7). This is the only destination for orders, and the deployment adds no database and no payment service.

Assumption: the file is served as a static file, so no server of Brew Lab's own is run.
Assumption: the LLD gives the detail of how the form delivers the order to hello@brewlab.example.

W-13.body:
## Risks

These risks come from the brief and the PRD. Each has a mitigation. None adds a fact beyond the brief. Claims about how the page is checked or changed are listed as assumptions after the table.

| Risk | What could go wrong | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overflow on phones | The page is wider than the screen, so customers must scroll sideways to read the menu or fill in the form (R10). | The phone layout (C6) is built so the page has no horizontal overflow at 360px width. See the assumption on the 360px width check. |
| Order does not reach the Shop team | The pre-order is not delivered to hello@brewlab.example, so the Shop team never sees it (R7). The page is one static file with no server code of its own. | The only destination for orders is hello@brewlab.example, and the LLD gives the detail of how the form delivers it. See the assumption on the test submission. |
| Wrong or missing order details | The customer leaves out the name, phone, items or pickup time, so the Shop team cannot prepare the order (R6). | The form has exactly these four fields and no others. See the assumptions on field labels and required fields. |
| Pickup time and undecided hours | Opening hours are not decided yet and are not shown (R11), so a customer may ask for a pickup time the shop cannot meet. | The page shows no opening hours. The form's pickup time is the time the customer asks for. See the assumptions on the pickup time wording and on changes once the hours are decided. |
| Hours or a shop phone number shown by mistake | An opening hours line or a shop phone number is added to the page, or the form's phone field is read as a shop phone number (R11). | The guard for page content (C7) keeps both off the page. The form's phone field is for the phone of the person ordering. |
| Expectation of online payment | A customer expects to pay on the page, but no online payment is taken and the page has no payment fields (R9). | The pickup and payment notice (C5) says that the order is collected at the shop (R8) and that no payment is taken online. |
| Documents and page disagree | The PRD, HLD, LLD and page differ on a name, address, price or form field (R12). | Every fact comes from the PRD: the seven menu items and prices (R4, R5), the address (R2) and the form fields (R6). See the assumption on the check before the file ships. |
| Menu price changes | A price on the page no longer matches the shop's price. | A price change is a change to the one file. See the assumption on changes to the file. |

Assumption: a test submission is checked against hello@brewlab.example before the file ships.
Assumption: each form field is labelled, so the customer knows what to enter.
Assumption: a failed 360px width check blocks the file from shipping.
Assumption: before the file ships, it is checked against the PRD for the seven menu items and prices, the address and the form fields.
Assumption: a price change, or a decision on opening hours, is made in the one file together with the PRD, HLD and LLD and checked again before the file replaces the earlier one.
Assumption: the form marks name, phone, items and pickup time as required fields, so an order is not sent with a field left empty.
Assumption: the page words the pickup time as a time the customer asks for, not a time the shop has confirmed.
